== Biography ==
Joseph was born in 1783, in Rockbridge County, Virgnia. He was the son of [[Glasgow-649|Arthur Glasgow]] and [[McNutt-600|Rebecca Anderson McNutt]].

An agreement dated 19 September 1822 concerning Arthur Glasgow's estate identifies Joseph among Arthur's children and devisees.<ref name="ArthurEstate1822">Arthur Glasgow estate agreement, 19 September 1822; [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/163-Rockbridge/BOX%20016/163_1833_005_0089.pdf Library of Virginia image].</ref> Alexander Brown's 1895 family history independently identifies Joseph as a son of Arthur and Rebecca Anderson McNutt Glasgow.<ref name="Brown1895">Alexander Brown, ''The Cabells and Their Kin'' (Boston: Houghton, Mifflin and Company, 1895), pp. 292–293; [https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=BAo7AAAAMAAJ&printsec=frontcover&output=reader&hl=en&pg=GBS.PA292 digital copy].</ref>

During the War of 1812, was served in the Rockbridge Light Horse Cavalry under Col. James Mcdowell, 5th Regiment, Virginia Militia<ref>https://www.fold3.com/image/307590369</ref>. 

On 26 Feb 1816, he married [[McCulloch-655|Nancy Ellis McCulloch]]<ref>https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6JZ7-M4Q8</ref>. They had two children.
#[[Glasgow-650|Rebecca Glasgow]] b. 1817 - d. 1837, age 20
#[[Glasgow-651|Elizabeth A Glasgow]] b. 1819 - d. aft. 1895, m. Hobson Johns

Joseph lived in Rockbridge throughout his life, where he was a farmer. It is here he passed away in 1856, age 73, from "disease of kidney"<ref>https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6ZR1-ZN5F</ref>. He is buried at the Oak Grove Cemetery.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-649]] is assessed at 99% (proved). Arthur’s 1822 estate agreement names Joseph among his children and devisees. Brown’s family history also identifies Joseph with Arthur and Rebecca McNutt, matching the Joseph born in 1783.

The estate relationship supports Arthur’s paternity directly; maternal details have their own source basis.

Next useful test: Resolve any estate-name ambiguity against the agreement and Joseph’s signatures.

Source basis already held: [https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/163-Rockbridge/BOX%20016/163_1833_005_0089.pdf Arthur Glasgow estate agreement, 19 September 1822; Library of Virginia image (https://old.lva.virginia.gov/ChanceryImg/163-Rockbridge/BOX%20016/163_1833_005_0089.pdf).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
